counterfactual_missing_items: No intracranial extension or adjacent soft-tissue mass to suggest a more aggressive/invasive process
No reported lucent/honeycomb or sunburst pattern for hemangioma
No elevated alkaline phosphatase or polyostotic involvement for Paget's disease
decisive_items: hyperostotic lesion of the outer table of the right calvarium
low signal intensity on T1- and T2-weighted images
response.rationale: R3 best fits the raw imaging description: a hyperostotic, densely calcified calvarial mass with low T1/T2 signal and no soft-tissue or dural extension is classic for osteoma. C1 is a correlated append-only completion of R3 using the same raw support span, so it is discounted. R5 and R4 rely on nonspecific hyperostosis but are contradicted by the dense calcified imaging pattern and missing systemic or vascular features. R1 only explains ancillary mastoid fluid and pain, not the dominant calcified bone lesion.

rejected.why: Correlated append-only completion of R3 with no additional raw support span beyond the same hyperostotic calvarium quote; discounted as a restatement.
Shares hyperostosis and inner-table thickening, but the discrete densely calcified low-T1/T2 mass in a young patient without metabolic or polyostotic findings argues strongly against Paget's disease.
Calvarial hemangioma would typically appear more lucent/honeycomb and vascular; the densely calcified, low-T1/T2 mass with no soft-tissue component is not supportive.
Mastoid pain, swelling, and fluid are ancillary findings; mastoiditis does not explain the dominant hyperostotic densely calcified bone lesion.
